info.title: Halite Developer API
info.summary: Permissioned shopper context for commerce apps and agents.
info.description:
Read what a consumer has chosen to share — preferences, interests, what they own and how it worked — after they approve your app on Halite's consent screen.

**Two credentials.** Your *secret key* (`hk_test_…` / `hk_live_…`) identifies your app. A consumer's *access token* (`hla_…`), from the OAuth flow, is what lets you read that consumer. A secret key alone never reads consumer data.

**Test first.** Test keys reach only six sandbox personas, never a real person.

post.summary: Send what they did in your app
post.description:
Tell Halite what this consumer viewed, saved, added to cart, bought, returned, rated or searched for — up to 100 events at a time. Each event needs your own `id` (sending it again changes nothing, so retries are safe) and a `category` the consumer shared with you (`category_not_granted` otherwise). Include the product’s `attributes` and `ingredients`: they are what enriches the profile.

Events enrich the profile every app and brand reads, de-identified: what the products were made of and how they went, the categories they shop, how fast they rebuy. Only your app sees its events as named products. Searches are stored but never used. The consumer can see what you sent; disconnecting stops new events and keeps what was sent.

Requires the `context.write` scope. Live, needs the Consumer Context plan or higher; never billed.

post.summary: Report merchants’ products you showed them
post.description:
Tell Halite which products from merchants on Halite you showed this consumer — by Halite `product_id`, or `merchant` slug and `sku` — up to 50 at a time. Each comes back with a tracked `url`: send the shopper there instead of the product page. Following it records the click and redirects them to the product; if they buy it from that merchant within 30 days, the sale is credited to your app in the merchant’s dashboard. Live only (test keys get the plain product link and nothing is recorded). Never billed.

Works with any valid access token. Live, needs the Identity & Consent (free) plan or higher; never billed.

post.summary: Score every product for this consumer
post.description:
Send up to 500 of your products; get every one back, best first, each with a match score, one sentence on why, and flags: `over_budget` (above what they usually spend in that category — shown, never dropped: it may be the one that solves for them), `avoid` (holds something they must not have) and `in_stock`. Nothing is left out. The top `picks` are marked `best_pick` — never one they must avoid or cannot buy now — and `per_type` keeps those varied. Costs 2 intelligence units.

Requires the `preferences.read` scope. Live, needs the Context Intelligence plan or higher; counted in intelligence units.

post.summary: What they are running out of
post.description:
From how fast they go through each kind of product (`context.read`) and, with `purchases.read`, when they last bought one: what is due within `within_days` or overdue, with a date and a confidence. Send your products to get the same product first, then the best alternatives of the same kind. When there is not enough to go on, `sufficient_data` is false and `reason` says why. Costs 2 intelligence units.

Requires the `context.read` scope. Live, needs the Context Intelligence plan or higher; counted in intelligence units.

post.summary: Turn what they typed into filters
post.description:
Interprets a shopper’s request — “something for dry patches under $30, nothing scented” — into categories, product types, concerns, ingredients to avoid and a price ceiling, filled in from their profile where the request is silent. `sources` marks each filter as from the request, the profile or both. Fixed rules come first; a model is only a backup, used when the rules cannot tell what is being looked for (`interpreted_by` says which). When they are shopping for someone else, their own profile is left out. Categories they asked for but have not shared with your app are listed in `not_shared`. Costs 5 intelligence units.

Requires the `preferences.read` scope. Live, needs the Context Intelligence plan or higher; counted in intelligence units.

secretKey.description: Your secret key: `hk_test_…` or `hk_live_…`. Server-side only.

clientBasic.description: Client id as username, secret key as password.

scope.description: What the consumer approved, which may be less than you asked.

consumer_id.description: Stable for your app; no other app sees the same id.

skin.description: The face. Granted with beauty.skincare, beauty.body or beauty.sun_care.

concerns.description: Everything they named, main concern first.

primary_concern.description: What they said they are most trying to change.

concerns.description: Everything they named, main concern first.

primary_concern.description: What they said they are most trying to change.

body.description: Body care, separate from the face. Granted with beauty.body.

texture.description: The texture they reach for, e.g. lotion, rich cream.

scent.description: How scented they like body care, e.g. unscented, lightly scented, strongly scented.

concerns.description: Everything they named, main concern first.

primary_concern.description: What they said they are most trying to change.

handle_with_care.description: Ingredients to keep from them, or to flag, and why. `allergy` and `avoids` should never be recommended; `reacts` can be, with a warning.

tensions.description: Two things they said that pull against each other, e.g. strongly scented body care with reactive skin. Shared only when you may see every category involved.

confidence.description: 0–1: how much there is to go on — what they stated, own and rated.

budgets.description: What they spend per product, per granted category.

id.description: Your id for the event, unique within your app.

occurred_at.description: When it happened: within the last year, not in the future.

category.description: Must be a category the consumer shared with your app.

attributes.description: What it is like: "fragrance-free", "gel", "ceramides". Shared with other apps de-identified; never its name or brand.

currency.description: ISO code; budgets are converted into it.

category.description: A category key such as beauty.skincare, so concerns and budgets match the right part of their profile.

product_type.description: Serum, shampoo, body butter… Used to keep recommendations varied and to match replenishment.

concerns.description: What the product is for, in any words: "dark spots", "dryness".

missing_quiz.description: Their quiz for this product’s category is missing or barely started: ask them to take it. `match` is null then.

picks.description: How many to mark as best picks. Every product is returned either way.

per_type.description: At most this many best picks of one product_type.

best_picks.description: Ids of the best picks, best first.

missing_quiz.description: Their quiz for this product’s category is missing or barely started: ask them to take it. `match` is null then.

why.description: The main reason, as one sentence for a product card.

over_budget.description: Above what they usually spend here. Informs; does not exclude.

products.description: Your products, to suggest the same one again or an alternative.

interpreted_by.description: Fixed rules always run first. A model fills in only when the rules cannot tell what is being looked for, and only fields they left empty.

not_shared.description: Categories the request named that the consumer has not shared with your app.

match.description: 0–100: how well it fits, measured only against what both their answers and your listing can speak to. Null when `missing_quiz` is set.

missing_quiz.description: Their quiz for this product’s category is missing or barely started: ask them to take it. `match` is null then.

avoid.description: Holds something they avoid or are allergic to: do not recommend.
